did_you_know.text: Did you know? The vision of the dry bones begins when the LORD’s hand comes upon Ezekiel, and he is brought by the Spirit into a valley full of bones.
Did you know? When the LORD asks Ezekiel whether the bones can live, the prophet humbly replies, “Only You know.”
Did you know? The process of restoration in the vision occurs in stages: tendons, flesh, skin, and then the spirit—only afterward does life return to the bodies.
Did you know? After the bones come together and tendons, flesh, and skin form over them, there is still no spirit in them; this emphasizes that life depends on the divine Spirit.
Did you know? When the spirit enters the bodies, they come to life, stand on their feet, and become a vast army.
Did you know? The LORD explains the vision Himself: the bones represent the whole house of Israel, which describes its condition with the words, “Our bones are dried up” and “Our hope is lost.”
Did you know? The purpose of the restoration is not merely renewed life, but also the return of the people to their own land, so that they will know that the LORD has spoken and acted.
Did you know? The two sticks symbolize the two parts of the people: one stick for Judah and one for Joseph, identified here with Ephraim and the tribes of Israel associated with him.
Did you know? The vision of reunification promises that the Israelites will no longer be two nations and two kingdoms, but one nation in the land, ruled by one king.
Did you know? In the future described in this chapter, there will be “one shepherd” over all the people, and the chapter calls this king “David My servant.”
